newsitem.title: USA: CBOT Nov soybeans seen down 10-20 cents, July up.
newsitem.headline: CBOT Nov soybeans seen down 10-20 cents, July up.

text.p: CBOT November soybean futures were called to open 10 to 20 cents per bushel lower on Monday after the U.S. Agriculture Department predicted 1997 soybean acreage would reach 70.85 million acres, traders said.
But July futures were called to open five to 10 cents per bushel higher on USDA quarterly stocks figures which came in at the lowest level since 1989.
USDA's soybean acreage estimate would make this year's planted area the largest since 1982. Analysts had expected the report to show 68.4 million acres planted.
But June 1 quarterly stocks figures were deemed bullish.
USDA put stocks at 499 million bushels, below trade expectations for 516 million bushels.
Project A overnight trade was up five cents per bushel to down two cents.
